title: Semi-automated extraction of information on open datasets mentioned in articles
author: Anastasiia Iarkaeva
materials: Copy each sub-extraction individually into the final copy.
New admin user in MySQL Fig. 10.4.

steps.title: Install Numbat Software
steps.instruction: Set up the Numbat environment on a Windows OS to manage the extraction database.

substeps.instruction: Install the XAMPP package (version 8.1.5) to provide Apache HTTP Server and MySQL Database.
Clone the Numbat repository from GitHub and copy the entire folder into the XAMPP 'htdocs' folder.
Start the Apache and MySQL modules in XAMPP.
Create a new MySQL database for Numbat and a new admin user account.
Complete the installation via the Apache admin window by entering the database username, password, name, host, and URL name.

steps.title: Collate Article Identifiers
steps.instruction: Create a list of article identifiers (typically DOIs) for assessment.

substeps.instruction: Search publication databases (e.g., Pubmed, Web of Science, OpenAlex, Dimensions, Embase) using criteria such as institutional affiliations, research fields, journals, and publication date ranges.
Export results with relevant metadata fields or obtain curated lists from institutional libraries.

steps.title: Retrieve Article Full Texts
steps.instruction: Obtain and store the full-text versions of the collated articles.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve texts via PubMed Central, unpaywall API, Publisher APIs (Elsevier, Wiley, Springer/Nature), or the full-text R package.
Store all retrieved full-texts in a single folder as PDFs (preferred) or text files (e.g., XML).

steps.title: Install and Configure ODDPub in R
steps.instruction: Set up the ODDPub text-mining algorithm in R (e.g., using RStudio).

substeps.instruction: Install the package using: install.packages("devtools") and devtools::install_github("quest-bih/oddpub")
Set the working directory to the folder containing the publications (e.g., setwd("C:\Users\username\path\to\PDFs")).
Create a new folder to store converted text files.

steps.title: Run ODDPub Screening
steps.instruction: Execute the ODDPub algorithm to detect data sharing statements and keywords.

substeps.instruction: Run the script using library(tidyverse) and library(oddpub).
Convert PDFs to text using oddpub::pdf_convert("PDFs/", "PDFs_to_text/").
Process the text and write the results to a CSV file: write_csv(oddpub_results, "oddpub_results.csv").

steps.title: Prepare Data for Numbat Import
steps.instruction: Filter and format the ODDPub output for manual validation in Numbat.

substeps.instruction: Filter the 'is_open_data' column to include only TRUE statements using a text editor (preferred over Excel to avoid data corruption).
Save the filtered data as a .tsv (tab-delimited) file.

steps.title: Configure Numbat Extraction Form
steps.instruction: Set up the manual verification questionnaire in Numbat.

substeps.instruction: Navigate to 'Edit extraction form' and click 'Import an extraction form'.
Import the extraction form in JSON format (Version 4).
Adjust conditions for question visibility as needed.

steps.title: Import Data and Assign Tasks
steps.instruction: Upload the filtered article list to Numbat and assign them to extractors.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'Manage reference sets' and click 'Add new reference set'.
Select relevant columns (e.g., doi, is_open_data, open_data_statement, is_reuse) and name the set.
Upload the .tsv file.
Go to 'Manage extraction assignments', select the records and the 'Openness' extraction form, and assign them to specific users.

steps.title: Perform Manual Data Extraction
steps.instruction: Manually verify the Open Data status of the detected statements.

substeps.instruction: Select 'Do extractions' and click 'Extract' for records where 'is_open_data' = TRUE.
Access the publication via doi.org or http://doi.org/ + DOI.
Review detected statements for repository info or accession codes, noting potential false positives (e.g., open code).
For each repository mentioned, add a new sub-extraction and extract one dataset.
Complete the form and click 'Complete'.
If the status is 'unsure', use the 'Assign to' option to reassign the dataset to another extractor.

steps.title: Perform Supplemental Manual Search
steps.instruction: Search for Open Data statements missed by the ODDPub algorithm.

substeps.instruction: Search for keywords: 'data availability', 'data sharing', and 'data access'.
If no specific section is found, search for 'dataset', 'data set', 'access*', and 'availab*'.
If still not found, search for 'data'; if results are > 10, dismiss them.

steps.title: Reconcile and Export Results
steps.instruction: Consolidate findings from multiple extractors and export the final report.

substeps.instruction: Go to 'Reconcile finished extractions' and compare answers from different extractors.
Discuss differing responses or use a 'master extractor' to make the final decision.
Copy each sub-extraction individually to the final report and click 'Completed'.
Go to 'Export data' -> 'Export Openness extractions' to download the .csv results table.
Clean the table in Excel using 'Text to Columns' (Delimited by tab/comma).
